title: Tanzanian Goat Soup
community: A beloved nourishing soup enjoyed across Tanzania
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Supu ya Mbuzi — Tanzanian goat soup. Goat bones and meat simmered for 2 hours with vegetables, ginger, and spices into a deeply rich, golden, nourishing broth. Tanzania's most restorative soup — believed to cure anything that ails you.
longDesc: Supu ya Mbuzi is Tanzania's most restorative food — the goat soup that is given to new mothers, the sick, and those recovering from hardship. The goat bones produce a gelatinous, golden broth of extraordinary nourishment. Every traditional healer recommends it.
steps: Blanch goat pieces in boiling water 5 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Place in pot with all vegetables, garlic, ginger, and spices.
Bring to a boil. Skim foam.
Strain. Shred any meat. Return to broth.
Garnish with coriander. Serve with lemon.
chefTips: Blanching produces a much clearer, cleaner broth.
Lowest possible simmer — never boil hard.
Lemon at the table is essential.
cookingScience: See TZA034 for bone broth cooking science. Goat bones are particularly collagen-rich around the joints — producing an especially gelatinous, nourishing broth.
sustainabilityTips: Uses bones that would otherwise be discarded.
healthBenefits: Rich in collagen, gelatin, and bone minerals.
culturalNote: Supu ya Mbuzi is Tanzania's healing food — the soup that new mothers receive after birth, that the sick are given when medicine has not worked, and that is believed to restore strength when all else has failed.
